front: la tête / le cou / l'épaule
context: Body parts usually take le/la, not my/your: 'J'ai mal à la tête'.

front: le bras / la main / le doigt
context: 'Le doigt' is pronounced [DWAH]: the g and t are silent.

front: la jambe / le genou / le pied
context: Plural: les genoux (with an x).

front: le dos / le ventre / la gorge
context: 'Le ventre' = belly/stomach; 'l'estomac' is the organ.

front: les yeux / le nez / la bouche / les dents
pronunciation: [lay ZYUH / luh NAY / lah BOOSH / lay DAHN]
context: Irregular plural: un œil → des yeux.

front: J'ai mal au dos.
context: 'Avoir mal à' + body part: au dos, à la tête, aux dents.

front: Où est-ce que vous avez mal ?
context: The doctor's first question.

front: J'ai de la fièvre depuis hier.
back: I've had a fever since yesterday.
context: 'Depuis' + present tense = since/for (still ongoing).

front: J'ai le nez qui coule.
context: Literally 'I have the nose that runs'.

front: Je tousse beaucoup la nuit.
back: I cough a lot at night.
context: 'Tousser' = to cough; 'la toux' = a cough.

front: Je crois que j'ai attrapé la grippe.
pronunciation: [zhuh krwah kuh zhay ah-trah-pay lah GREEP]
back: I think I've caught the flu.
context: 'Attraper' = to catch. 'Un rhume' = a cold.

front: Je me sens mal, j'ai la nausée.
pronunciation: [zhuh muh sahn MAHL, zhay lah noh-ZAY]
context: 'Se sentir' + adverb: je me sens bien / mal / mieux.

front: Je voudrais prendre rendez-vous chez le médecin.
pronunciation: [zhuh voo-dreh prahn-druh rahn-day-VOO shay luh mayd-SAN]
back: I'd like to make an appointment with the doctor.
context: Many appointments are booked online in France (for example on Doctolib).

front: Vous avez votre carte Vitale ?
back: Do you have your Carte Vitale?
context: The green health insurance card used in France to get reimbursed.

front: Le médecin m'a fait une ordonnance.
back: The doctor wrote me a prescription.
context: 'Une ordonnance' = prescription. Take it to 'la pharmacie'.

front: Prenez ce médicament trois fois par jour.
pronunciation: [pruh-nay suh may-dee-kah-MAHN trwah fwah par ZHOOR]
back: Take this medicine three times a day.
context: 'Un médicament' = medicine (the product); 'la médecine' = the science.

front: Je me suis cassé le bras en skiant.
pronunciation: [zhuh muh swee kah-SAY luh BRAH ahn skee-YAHN]
context: Reflexive with body parts: 'se casser le bras' (not 'mon bras').

front: Je me suis coupé le doigt.
context: 'Se couper' = to cut oneself. 'Un pansement' = a bandage/plaster.

front: Il faut aller aux urgences.
back: We need to go to the emergency room.
context: 'Les urgences' = ER. Emergency numbers: 15 (medical), 112 (Europe-wide).

front: Je suis allergique à la pénicilline.
context: Always mention allergies to doctors and pharmacists.

front: Ça va mieux aujourd'hui ?
context: 'Mieux' = better (adverb). 'Je vais mieux' = I'm feeling better.

front: Prompt rétablissement !
context: Formal. Informally: 'Soigne-toi bien !' (take care of yourself).

front: Je fais attention à ce que je mange.
pronunciation: [zhuh feh zah-tahn-SYOHN ah suh kuh zhuh MAHNZH]
context: 'Faire attention à' = to be careful about, pay attention to.

front: Il faut boire au moins un litre et demi d'eau par jour.
pronunciation: [eel foh bwahr oh mwan an lee-truh ay duh-MEE DOH par ZHOOR]
back: You should drink at least one and a half liters of water a day.
context: 'Il faut' + infinitive = one must. 'Au moins' = at least.

front: Je dors mal depuis quelques semaines.
back: I haven't been sleeping well for a few weeks.
context: 'Dormir' (je dors) is irregular. 'L'insomnie' = insomnia.

front: Je suis stressé à cause du travail.
pronunciation: [zhuh swee streh-SAY ah kohz dü trah-VAHY]
context: 'À cause de' + noun = because of (negative cause). 'Grâce à' = thanks to (positive).

front: Je fais du yoga pour me détendre.
pronunciation: [zhuh feh dü yoh-GAH poor muh day-TAHN-druh]
context: 'Se détendre' = to relax.

front: J'ai arrêté de fumer il y a un an.
pronunciation: [zhay ah-reh-tay duh fü-MAY eel yah an NAHN]
back: I quit smoking a year ago.
context: 'Arrêter de' + infinitive = to stop doing. 'Il y a' + time = ago.

front: Tu as mauvaise mine, tu es fatigué ?
pronunciation: [tü ah moh-vez MEEN, tü eh fah-tee-GAY]
back: You don't look well, are you tired?
context: 'Avoir bonne mine / mauvaise mine' = to look well / unwell.

front: Je me suis tordu la cheville.
context: 'La cheville' = ankle; 'le poignet' = wrist.

front: Le dentiste m'a dit de revenir dans six mois.
pronunciation: [luh dahn-TEEST mah dee duh ruh-vuh-NEER dahn see MWAH]
back: The dentist told me to come back in six months.
context: 'Dire de' + infinitive = to tell (someone) to do.

front: La pharmacie de garde est ouverte toute la nuit.
pronunciation: [lah far-mah-SEE duh GARD eh too-vehrt toot lah NWEE]
back: The on-duty pharmacy is open all night.
context: Look for the green cross. 'De garde' = on duty.

front: Il faut que tu te reposes.
context: 'Il faut que' + subjunctive. Here 'reposes' looks like the present.

front: Je n'ai pas de mutuelle.
back: I don't have supplementary health insurance.
context: 'La mutuelle' tops up what the Sécurité sociale reimburses. Most employees get one through work.

front: Elle est enceinte de six mois.
context: 'Enceinte' = pregnant. False friend: 'pregnant' is never 'prégnante'.
